text:
Maria: hey team — pushed a first pass of updated internal incident comms templates to the docs repo. want quick feedback before i propagate to oncall playbooks. main goals: consistent tone, clear placeholders, and short customer-safe blurbs we can drop into status page + emails. :memo:
Alex: nice, thanks. can you paste the key sections here? quick skim will help.
Maria: sure — i pasted three examples below: (1) internal update, (2) customer notification, (3) status page snippet. please flag anything that feels too technical or too vague.
Maria: INTERNAL UPDATE TEMPLATE:
```
Severity: SEV-2
Summary: short 1-line description of issue
Impact: who/how many customers/systems affected
Current status: what we've done so far + current mitigation
Next steps / owner: who's driving the workaround / next action and ETA
Customer-facing note: short phrase for status page / support reps
Tags: services impacted, region, root-cause hypothesis
```
Jamal: love the structure. suggestion: add a "Customer Risk" line (low/medium/high) so support knows escalation level.
Sophie: +1 on that. also recommend a "Clear when to update" guideline — e.g., update internal every 15m for sev1, 30m for sev2, or on state changes.
Maria: good call — i'll add Customer Risk and cadence. also added placeholders like <SERVICE>, <ESTIMATE_RESTORE>, <WORKAROUND_LINK>. keep them ALL CAPS so ppl don't accidentally send them.
incident-bot: paging @oncall (Alex) — new thread created: "comm-template-refresh" — please acknowledge.
Alex: acknowledged. reading now. :eyes:
Alex: one tone question: for customer-facing copy do we prefer "We are currently investigating" vs "We're aware and investigating"? the latter feels more active.
Elaine: i'd prefer "We are currently investigating" for higher formality in emails; shorter for status page can be "Investigating". keep email -> full sentences, status -> telegraphic.
Maria: noted. adopting: email = full sentences, status page = short fragments. adding examples: 
CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE:
```
Subject: [Redwood] Incident impacting <SERVICE> in <REGION>
Hi <CUSTOMER_NAME>,
We are currently investigating an issue affecting <SERVICE> in <REGION>. Some requests may experience increased latencies or errors. Our on-call team is actively working on a fix and we will provide an update by <ESTIMATE_RESTORE>.
Workaround: <WORKAROUND_LINK> (if applicable)
Status page: <STATUS_PAGE_LINK>
We apologize for the disruption — please reply to this thread if you need immediate assistance.
Thanks,
Redwood Support
```
Sophie: maybe add a line about data integrity if relevant: e.g., "There is no indication of data loss" or "We're investigating potential data impact" — but only if engineering confirms.
Maria: yes — separate checkbox in template: [ ] Confirmed: no data loss (yes/no/unknown).
Jamal: for status page snippet, we should keep token budget tight. sample: 
STATUS PAGE SNIPPET:
```
Investigating — We are aware of an issue affecting <SERVICE> in <REGION> causing increased latency and occasional 5xx. Our team is working on a fix. Updated <ESTIMATE_RESTORE>.
```
Alex: also add a "what we tried" one-liner for internal updates so follow-on shifts know what's been attempted. helps avoid duplicate work.
Maria: added: "Mitigations attempted" short bullet list.
incident-bot: reminder — oncall handoff scheduled in 30m: @Alex -> @Jamal. please complete handoff checklist.
Alex: copying handoff checklist here: 
HANDOFF CHECKLIST:
```
- Current hypothesis and evidence
- Live mitigations in place (links to runbooks / playbooks)
- Remaining risks and next actions
- Contact points (pager, slack, phone)
- Customer comms already sent (links)
- Open support tickets summary
```
Elaine: can we standardize the "customer impact" phrasing? sometimes support writes "some customers" which is too vague. propose: use one of these: "All customers in <REGION>", "Subset of customers using <FEATURE>", "Intermittent errors for a small percentage of requests".
Maria: excellent — i'll add a small library of approved impact sentences to copy from. will include severity crosswalk (sev1->global outage wording, sev2->partial-impact wording).
Jamal: quick note on approvals: any customer-facing email must be signed off by the incident commander + support lead before send. add a checkbox in template.
Sophie: for tone — recommend "calm, clear, and accountable". avoid overpromising recovery times. use placeholders like <ESTIMATE_RESTORE> not exact if unsure.
Maria: agreed. final item: localization. we need a short note in templates reminding CS to localize or escalate to localization team for non-English customers.
Alex: nit: put a short example of a 'status page update timeline' at the top of template, e.g., 
"T+0: acknowledge, T+15: initial details, T+60: incident analysis, T+? restore" — helps set expectations.
Maria: added. ok i will push updated markdown later today and ping the #oncall handbook channel. thanks for the quick review — any other items?
Elaine: can you include a short "Do not disclose" list? (e.g., internal root cause details not confirmed, sensitive customer data).
Maria: yup adding.
ops-bot: note: new doc created at https://redwood.internal/docs/incidents/comms-templates (edit access: incident-owners group)
Alex: perfect. i'll test the customer template in the staging status page flow later and report back.
Maria: great — if no objections i'll merge in ~4 hours. :thumbsup:
